@cmlh, please have discussion here in the issue first, and if the change/proposal found agreement, then it's time to make PR. Discussion over pull-requests is just a mess. Discussion in PR should be targeted only for "syntax or language", not for the idea of the change itself. This is also stated in PR template.

To address @tghosth https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/979#issuecomment-839434790

> Given that 9.1.3 already mandates TLS 1.2 and 1.3, I am not sure I am clear on what is being added on 9.1.5.

Pull Request https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/pull/983 specifies the addition of 9.1.5 mandates the server side control exclude TLS 1.2 after TLS 1.3 support is released by the specific web technologies. 

> Also, I'm not sure that server side support is as important as client side support which I think is the biggest problem in deprecating versions of TLS. I agree that we should be whatever possible mandating the best possible security controls but we also have to be realistic because the more controls we include which are impossible from a business perspective, the weaker the standard gets.

I am willing to add a check box to a changes/Issue Template that I have discussed with @elarlang to disclose if an ASVS change  impacts client side support of deprecating web technologies, such as for [TLS 1.2](https://caniuse.com/tls1-2), etc.

However, we would also need consensus that ASVS now extends to the client side too? 

> Perhaps the best option would be a note within 9.1.3 that companies should expect and be ready for deprecations of TLS versions?

These are most recent mandates tracked within https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/979#issuecomment-836452364

- TLS 1.2 from March 31, 2021
- TLS 1.3 from January 1, 2024

I support inserting a note to document the above as proposed by @tghosth 

> Also, as a general note (which I am not sure is documented anywhere), we don't like to include links within requirements (the links to the proactive controls are an exception which we are planning to remove in the next major release).

No problem, I recommended this be explored with the OWASP Testing Guide within https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/992#issue-883840380 I just need to anchor it somewhere before Issue #992 is transferred. 

I also document this within the amended Issues and Pull Request Template(s) that I am working on.

@randomstuff wrote:
> This implicitly makes TLS 1.2 somewhat into the **Legacy** status.

The quote relevant to TLS 1.2 from [5.0 Appendix C Cryptography](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x92-Appendix-C_Cryptography.md) is reproduced below:
>MAC-then-encrypt is still allowed for compatibility with legacy applications. It is used in TLS v1.2 with old ciphers suites.

Yes, the only reason to deprecate TLS 1.2 (as in, advise for it being disabled) is when the only key-exchanges we accept are the post-quantum ones, as those can't be used in TLS 1.2. At least, as far as predictable things go.

Until there's X25519 and P-256 in allowed groups for TLS 1.3, there's no reason to remove TLS 1.2 from "acceptable provided good configuration".
